name: Crossing the Rubicon
description: A piece whose primary origin is on the opponent's half cannot return to the affected player's half.
ambiguities: Opponent half is ranks 5-8 for White and 1-4 for Black. Location is authoritative even for custom starting FENs; castling uses the logged king move.

name: True Love
description: King destinations must be adjacent to an own queen, and queen destinations must be adjacent to the own king.
ambiguities: Any promoted own queen may satisfy the king condition. Promotions are pawn moves; castling evaluates the king destination.

name: Lethal Attraction
description: The primary mover cannot finish farther from the opponent king than it started.
ambiguities: Distance is Manhattan distance. Castling evaluates the primary king endpoints rather than the auxiliary rook.

name: Thunderdome
description: A piece cannot leave the middle sixteen squares while another piece remains there.
ambiguities: The dome is files c-f and ranks 3-6. 'Only piece' counts pieces of either color.

name: Irresistible
description: If possible, the affected player must move a previously non-adjacent piece adjacent to the opponent king.
ambiguities: The observed king-capture exception cannot execute because standard chess legality never generates king captures; endpoint forcing is fully implemented.

name: Prima Donna
description: A move cannot leave more than one affected-player pawn on any file.
ambiguities: The resulting-position invariant also requires a custom already-invalid position to be repaired. Promotion removes the pawn from the count.

name: Inside the Lines
description: A primary mover cannot enter the rim from a non-rim square.
ambiguities: Rim means files a/h or ranks 1/8. Rim-origin moves may remain on the rim or return inside.

name: Boxing with Shadow
description: If possible, the affected player must move to the origin square of the opponent's previous primary move.
ambiguities: Castling history uses the logged king origin; all qualifying ordinary moves remain available.

name: Cowardly
description: After the opponent captures, every legal response must move backward.
ambiguities: Backward is strict rank decrease for White and increase for Black. Same-rank moves and castling do not satisfy it.

name: Going the Distance
description: A move's Manhattan distance must be at least the Manhattan distance of the opponent's previous move.
ambiguities: Both moves use primary endpoints, including castling, promotion, and en-passant.

name: Left to Right
description: Destinations must progress to a file right of the affected player's previous destination until reaching the h-file.
ambiguities: Right is interpreted as absolute file progression a-to-h for both colors; the public wording does not clarify player-relative orientation.

name: Relay Race
description: If possible, the affected player must move a piece whose origin is adjacent to their previous destination.
ambiguities: Adjacency is measured before the move and includes diagonals. Castling history uses the king destination.

name: Religious Dispute
description: After the opponent moves a bishop, the affected player's next primary mover must be a bishop.
ambiguities: A pawn promotion to bishop remains a pawn move and neither triggers nor satisfies the response.

name: Simon Says
description: The affected player's destination must have the same square color as the opponent's previous destination.
ambiguities: Destination color uses a1 as dark; castling uses the king destination and en-passant the landing square.

name: Superstitious
description: The affected player cannot move to any destination where the opponent previously made a capture.
ambiguities: An en-passant capture curses the capturing pawn's landing square, not the removed pawn square.

name: Torpedos
description: After a quiet pawn move, the same physical piece must move again if it has an ordinary legal move.
ambiguities: Physical continuity follows a quiet promotion into its promoted piece; pawn captures do not trigger.

name: Stir Crazy
description: After four consecutive affected-player turns without moving the king, the fifth primary mover must be the king.
ambiguities: The window counts affected-player turns rather than plies. Castling is a king move and resets the streak.

name: Bloodthirsty
description: After three grace turns, two consecutive quiet turns force a capture on the next affected-player turn.
ambiguities: Detector observations say turns while the forum says rounds; the implementation counts affected-player turns. En-passant counts as a capture.

name: Fixation
description: Within the pawn or non-pawn category, the same physical piece remains focused until a move from the opposite category.
ambiguities: Promotion is a pawn move, after which moving the promoted piece switches to the non-pawn category. Castling focuses the king only.

name: Leveling Up
description: Capture targets unlock in order: pawn, knight, bishop, rook, queen, then king.
ambiguities: A predecessor need only have been captured previously; lower unlocked targets remain capturable. Standard chess never captures the king.

name: Quicksand
description: A piece that ends two consecutive own turns unchanged on rank four or five becomes permanently frozen.
ambiguities: Twice in a row means consecutive affected-player end-turn snapshots. Runtime continuity uses piece type and square with moved-destination replacement protection; castling tracks the rook separately. Exact state cannot be reconstructed from only a final FEN and move list, so midgame initialization requires supplied state.

name: Absolution
description: After a non-bishop captures, that physical piece cannot capture again until it starts a later turn adjacent to an own bishop.
ambiguities: A newly dirty piece adjacent to a bishop is absolved only at a later turn start. Capturing promotions use the pre-move pawn for the bishop exemption, so a promoted bishop remains dirty. Exact state cannot be reconstructed from only a final FEN and move list, so midgame initialization requires supplied state.

name: Moving Day
description: At the start of the twenty-first affected-player turn and later, no own piece may remain on its home rank.
ambiguities: The deadline counts twenty completed affected-player turns and includes pawns as pieces.

name: Siege
description: By the start of the twenty-first affected-player turn, the affected player must have captured a rook.
ambiguities: The loss is checked after twenty completed affected-player turns. A captured promoted rook counts by its current captured type.
